statement: A shop sells pencils for $30$ cents each, or in packs of $12$ for $\$3$. What is the greatest number of pencils Ana can buy with $\$10$?

choices.misconception: I worked out that Ana should buy 3 packs and gave the number of packs instead of the number of pencils.
I bought only single pencils at 30 cents, and 1000 / 30 is 33 with some money left over.
I bought 3 packs for 9 dollars but forgot to spend the last dollar on single pencils.
I thought every pencil costs 25 cents, the pack price, so 10 dollars buys 40, but pencils bought one at a time cost 30 cents.

hints: Which way of buying is cheaper per pencil?
A pack works out to $25$ cents a pencil. Buy as many packs as you can, then use what is left.
Three packs cost $\$9$ and give $36$ pencils. The last $\$1$ buys single pencils at $30$ cents each.

solutions.reliable: Packs cost $300 / 12 = 25$ cents per pencil, cheaper than $30$ cents, so buy as many packs as possible: $3$ packs for $\$9$ give $36$ pencils. The remaining $100$ cents buy $3$ more single pencils (with $10$ cents left). Checking the other options: $2$ packs leave $\$4$, which buys $13$ singles, for $37$; $1$ pack gives $12 + 23 = 35$; no packs gives $33$. The greatest is $39$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
